title: Transformer Architecture & Self-Attention Internals
description: Understand the neural mechanics of transformers, self-attention equations, decoder-only architectures, and KV caching for software engineers.

data.text: Introduced in the seminal 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need', the Transformer replaced recurrence (RNNs/LSTMs) and convolutions with self-attention mechanisms. While RNNs processed tokens sequentially from left to right—creating a computational bottleneck that prevented parallel training—transformers process all tokens in a sequence concurrently, enabling training across thousands of GPUs on trillions of tokens.

At the heart of every transformer block is the Scaled Dot-Product Attention mechanism. Every input token is projected into three distinct vector representations: Query (Q: what am I looking for?), Key (K: what do I contain?), and Value (V: what information do I pass along?):
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax( (Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k) ) * V

1. Dot product (Q * K^T) computes the raw similarity score between every pair of tokens in the sequence. 2. Scaling by sqrt(d_k) stabilizes gradients against vanishing/exploding values. 3. Softmax normalizes scores into probability distributions summing to 1.0. 4. Multiplying by V computes a weighted sum of values, blending context from all related tokens.

Translates source sequence into target sequence

data.text: The Engineering Reality of KV Caching

In decoder-only autoregressive generation, generating Token N requires attention across Tokens 0 through N-1. If the model had to recompute Query, Key, and Value vectors for all preceding tokens on every step, generation time would grow quadratically O(N^2). Modern inference engines (vLLM, Azure OpenAI, TensorRT-LLM) implement Key-Value (KV) Caching: previous K and V matrices are stored in GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM). This makes subsequent token generation O(1) in compute, but turns GPU VRAM into the primary memory bottleneck.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Transformers replace sequential recurrence with parallelizable self-attention
Scaled dot-product attention calculates dynamic semantic relationships: Q, K, and V
Modern generative LLMs (GPT, Llama) are predominantly Causal Decoder-Only architectures
Encoder-only models (like BERT) remain the gold standard for dense embedding generation
The KV Cache optimizes generation compute to O(1) per token but consumes significant GPU VRAM
data.takeaway: Understanding the transformer's inner mechanics—from self-attention matrices to KV caching—enables .NET engineers to optimize latency budgets, comprehend prompt pricing, and build resilient AI systems.
